Here's a paraphrase of the article excerpt:

In France, the social security program ensures that expectant and new mothers receive free medical care at government-run medical facilities. Women who work receive 16 weeks of leave after giving birth, during which they are paid between €9.29 and €84.90 daily, depending on their previous earnings. From a financial standpoint, the period surrounding pregnancy and birth doesn't create additional hardship compared to normal times: families with limited resources continue to face challenges as before, while those who are financially comfortable maintain their status.

However, when it comes to actual support for new mothers, there is very little assistance available. Fathers are only granted 11 days of leave, which doesn't even provide enough time for mothers to physically recover from delivery. Consequently, new mothers must handle the constant, round-the-clock responsibilities of caring for their newborn while simultaneously trying to recuperate. Additionally, they face the challenge of finding suitable childcare options, as government-provided programs are inadequate, particularly in the greater Paris area. Childcare expenses fluctuate significantly. At public daycare facilities, lower-income families might pay approximately €1,000 annually, though availability is extremely limited with only one spot available for every eight children. As a result, families turn to private alternatives like nannies or in-home caregivers.

Any other questions?
